Thought: We need to determine the type of molecule that results from the reaction of 4-Bromobenzoyl and pentanoic acid. 4-Bromobenzoyl suggests a benzoyl group with a bromine substituent at the para position. Pentanoic acid is a carboxylic acid. Typically, in organic chemistry, a reaction between an acyl halide (such as 4-Bromobenzoyl chloride) and a carboxylic acid can form an acid anhydride, an ester, or, less commonly, other functional groups. The most likely outcome, considering the reactants specified, is the formation of an ester. An ester forms when the hydroxyl group of the carboxylic acid reacts with the acyl group of the other reactant, releasing a molecule of HBr in this case.
